chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Mu'adh ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said:
Be patient with the enemies of blessings, for you will never deal with the one who has disobeyed God regarding you with anything better than obeying God regarding him.

key_terms.أعداء النعم: Enemies of blessings — those who, through jealousy or malice, oppose or undermine the blessings God has given to others
key_terms.تطيع الله فيه: To obey God regarding him — to maintain moral conduct toward someone even when they have wronged you
key_terms.تكافئ: To repay, deal with, or match someone in their actions

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say is the best way to respond to those who wrong you?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delivers a concise ethical teaching on the proper response to those who wrong us. Rather than seeking revenge or retaliation against those who harm us (described as 'enemies of blessings'), the Imam teaches that the most effective and noble response is to obey God in one's dealings with them. This reflects a core Shi'a ethical principle: wrongdoing should be met with righteousness, not reciprocal transgression.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
